statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 venues are in the weekend halt with Tail low and Stress high.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold. CME equity futures are halted until Sunday 22:00Z, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop within this horizon. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 enters the weekend halt at a record close, with Friday's completed retracement keeping Tail low while oil near $102 and a 5.28% 10-year hold Stress high
body: Friday 2 October ended with the Nasdaq-100 at a record 30,807.93, up 1.00%, but the close sat about 210 points below the 31,017.53 session high and only some 70 points above the low, so the session finished with its retracement completed rather than holding an extreme. VIX fell 6.59% to 15.31, settling at the bottom of its 15.30-16.24 range. September payrolls arrived at just 29,000 against a consensus near 84,000-90,000 with unemployment up to 4.2% and average hourly earnings at 0.1% month-on-month, which cut October Fed rate-hike odds from roughly 64% to about 16%. Yields nonetheless rose: the 10-year closed up around 5 basis points at 5.28% after an intraday low of 5.16%, and the 30-year added 2 basis points to 5.63%, leaving equities at a record while the long end firmed. That cross-asset conflict, together with Brent effectively flat at $102.25, WTI at $91.11 after an intraday one-month low of $88.06, record US pump prices near $6.53 a gallon, the continuing Strait of Hormuz closure and a G7 agreement to release up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel over four months, describes a difficult and unresolved macro environment. It is a Stress environment rather than Tail evidence: CME equity futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z and do not reopen until Sunday 22:00Z, so every hour of this forecast horizon lies inside the halt and no pathological price path can form. Shared Finviz context was older than its 90-minute freshness bound and was therefore excluded, with independent research used in its place.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span Friday's U.S. session and the start of the weekend halt. Claude history shows Tail easing from an orange 25-27 band around the 13:00-14:00Z U.S. cash open into a yellow 21-23 through the afternoon, then dropping to green single digits from 21:00Z as the cash close completed its retracement and CME futures went into the weekend halt. Stress stayed in the 65-79 high band throughout on the energy and yield backdrop, and Confidence held in the 82-89 range.
outlookSummary: Every hour of this horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, which began Friday 21:00Z and runs until the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop and Tail stays low and flat at 8-10 with the mapped state green throughout. Stress eases modestly from 65 to about 62 through the dead Saturday hours, then firms back toward 65 as the window advances with the Hormuz closure and the term-premium backdrop unresolved. Confidence decays gradually from 85 to 77 purely as Friday's verified evidence ages. The first genuine checkpoint, Monday's ISM Services PMI at 14:00Z, lies beyond this window, and any weekend escalation or G7 implementation news could only be expressed at the reopen, which is also outside it.
